title: TCP and UDP: ports, handshake and when to use each

videos.script: The internet layer delivers packets on a best effort. Some arrive late, some arrive out of order, and some never arrive at all. A web page cannot be built from most of its bytes. {{best}} TCP turns that into something a program can trust: a connection, where every byte arrives, in order, or the program is told it did not. It does it with numbers and acknowledgements, and with patience. {{tcp}} UDP does none of that. It sends one packet and forgets it. That sounds worse, and for a DNS question or a video call it is exactly right, because a late answer is no better than no answer. {{udp}} In this lesson you will watch a TCP connection open, carry a request and close, packet by packet. You will make the network lose one packet in five and see TCP deliver the file anyway. {{lab}} Then you will learn the three things a port can answer: yes, no, and nothing at all. Telling no from nothing is most of what a firewall problem looks like from the outside. {{answers}}
